niche: an intergovernmental liability risk pool setting its 2027 per-occurrence retention from the ground-up severity of its members' liability occurrences, where the law enforcement occurrences run a far longer tail than the other coverage parts and the actuary projects each group's 2027 frequency on its own exposure

driver: The decisive quantity is the upper tail of a size distribution made of two kinds of item whose tails differ by far more than their bulk, with the expected number above a low anchor projected separately for each kind; the record identifies both tails once each kind is fitted on its own through the record's floor and ceiling, and the count above each high threshold is the sum of each kind's anchor times its own tail ratio, while one curve fitted to the pooled record is shaped by the short-tailed majority and puts the dial two steps too low.
driver_concrete: Ground-up liability severity is fitted at 2027 cost to the pool's record of accident years 2014 to 2021, each occurrence left-truncated at its member's deductible and censored at the retention, separately for law enforcement liability and for the other four coverage parts, and the expected 2027 occurrences above each quoted attachment are the actuary's 85.5 law enforcement and 364.3 other occurrences above $25,000 each carried by its own curve: they first fall to one at $4.0 million (1.20 above $3.0 million, 0.83 above $4.0 million), while one curve fitted to every occurrence, the same likelihood, clears one at $2.0 million (0.92).
stump: The default path fits the policy's lognormal by maximum likelihood to every occurrence of 2014 to 2021, each truncated at its deductible and the 25 at the retention censored, both at 2027 cost, and carries the actuary's 449.8 occurrences above $25,000 by that one curve: $2.0 million (0.92 above it); the law enforcement occurrences, under a third of the record, carry most of the tail, and the one curve is shaped by the other parts; fitted for each group and summed over the actuary's two projections the count first clears one at $4.0 million (1.20 above $3.0 million, 0.83 above $4.0 million).
analyst_test: A strong analyst who cleans both loss runs, reads every field and filed rule, brings the record to 2027 cost and fits the lognormal by maximum likelihood with each deductible as truncation and the capped occurrences censored at the retention, then carries the actuary's total of 449.8 by that curve, files $2.0 million (0.92 above it); two isolated call-only probes did exactly that.
domain_test: The call turns on the ground-up severity tail of a public entity pool's liability occurrences at each excess attachment, estimated the way excess layers are priced, with severity curves by coverage (law enforcement liability against general, auto, public officials' and employment practices liability) fitted through the deductible-truncated, retention-censored record and weighted by the actuary's frequency projections on each coverage's own exposure; with another field's nouns there is no coverage part whose verdicts run a longer tail, no deductible floor, no retention ceiling and no excess attachment to set.

lineage.architecture: v1 (loop 0): the likelihood of the record on a window whose every occurrence had closed
lineage.fate: hardened at the author's request for a second layer (2026-10-13, before any portal result); kept as rung R3 of loop 1, where the suits past the retention stay open under the excess insurer's defence and the closed-file construction files $3.0 million
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the upper tail of a size distribution whose items reach the record only above a floor that differs from item to item and are recorded only up to a ceiling that moved during the record, so the fit has to carry each item's floor as truncation and the ceiling as censoring, both at the cost level the curve is fitted at; fitting the recorded sizes as a complete sample thins the tail and sets the dial two steps too low, and treating only the ceiling still leaves it a step and more short.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the upper tail of a size distribution whose items reach the record only above a floor that differs from item to item and are recorded only up to a ceiling that moved during the record, and whose largest items stay unfinished long after the small ones finish; the fit has to carry each item's floor as truncation and the ceiling as censoring at the fitted cost level over every item of the window, the unfinished ones included as the censored observations they are, because fitting only the finished items selects on size and thins the tail a step short, and fitting the recorded sizes as complete thins it more.
